title: PCOS Lifestyle Intervention Program
author: Geranne Jiskoot
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfq9jmz6
materials: The aim of this study is to examine whether CBT, provided by a mental health professional working in a multidisciplinary team with a dietician and a physical therapist (a three-component intervention), is effective to decrease weight, compared to usual care at the end of treatment in obese women with PCOS. Furthermore, we explore whether mobile phone applications are effective in supporting behavioural change and sustainable weight loss.
CBT provided by a multidisciplinary team or;
encouraging and promoting physical activity; and
a weight loss of 4.0 BMI points;

steps.title: Screen and Enroll Participants
steps.instruction: Screen women with menstrual cycle disorders using the CyclusOLigoAmenorroe (COLA) protocol and enroll eligible candidates.

substeps.instruction: Perform COLA protocol screening including family and reproductive history, anthropomorphometric, and ultrasonographic assessments.
Diagnose participants according to WHO classification and the Rotterdam consensus criteria for PCOS.
Provide detailed information on the role of weight loss in PCOS and lifestyle modification benefits via a patient information leaflet.
Contact patients by telephone after 2 weeks to assess willingness to participate.
Obtain signed informed consent forms via regular mail.

steps.title: Perform Baseline Assessment and Randomization
steps.instruction: Conduct initial measurements and assign participants to one of three study arms.

substeps.instruction: Perform baseline measurements.

Randomize participants at a 2:1 ratio using a computer-generated random numbers table into: 1-year CBT lifestyle intervention with SMS (n=78), 1-year CBT lifestyle intervention without SMS (n=78), or usual care control group (n=78).
Execute assignment using sequentially numbered, identical, sealed envelopes (A for SMS, B for non-SMS, C for control).

steps.title: Implement Multidisciplinary CBT Lifestyle Intervention
steps.instruction: Deliver a 1-year program consisting of 20 group sessions and individual counseling to change cognitions, dietary habits, physical activity, and social support.

substeps.instruction: Conduct 20 group sessions (max 10 patients per group), each 2.5 hours long: first 1.5 hours supervised by a mental health professional and dietician, and the final hour by a physical therapist.
Provide 5 individual counseling sessions (45 min each) with a mental health professional, 5 with a physical therapist, and 5 with a dietician.
Utilize the 'PCOS lifestyle textbook' for participants and the therapist manual (including PowerPoint slides) for standardization.

steps.title: Execute Intervention Phase 1 (Months 1-3)
steps.instruction: Conduct weekly group sessions (sessions 1-11) focusing on awareness and restructuring dysfunctional thoughts.

substeps.instruction: Apply CBT techniques to address thoughts regarding lifestyle, weight loss, and self-esteem.
Implement nutritional guidelines based on the Dutch food guide (DFG) for women aged 19-50, targeting a total intake of 2000 kcal (1700 kcal for main meals, 300 kcal for healthy snacking).
Encourage sustainable food choices and avoid restrained behaviors like skipping meals.
Prescribe physical activity per WHO guidelines: 5 days of moderate activity (30 min/day), vigorous exercise 1-3 days/week (min 20 min/session), and 8-10 muscle-strengthening activities twice weekly.

steps.title: Execute Intervention Phase 2 (Months 3-6)
steps.instruction: Conduct bi-weekly group sessions (sessions 12-16) to promote self-regulation.

substeps.instruction: Motivate participants to develop structured eating patterns to avoid binge eating or over-restriction.
Reinforce behavioral skills developed in Phase 1.
Decrease face-to-face contact frequency to stimulate proactive coping.

steps.title: Execute Intervention Phase 3 (Months 6-9)
steps.instruction: Conduct monthly group sessions (sessions 17-19) focusing on maintenance.

substeps.instruction: Teach relapse management and weight loss maintenance.
Set new goals for the following 3 months using proactive coping.
Schedule individual counseling sessions upon participant request.

steps.title: Execute Intervention Phase 4 (Months 9-12)
steps.instruction: Provide a final group session (session 20) and transition to an outreach-based support model.

substeps.instruction: Conduct the 20th group session.
Allow participants to contact the multidisciplinary team for individual counseling as needed.
Maintain an outreach policy to ensure attendance at measurement sessions.

steps.title: Administer SMS Maintenance Support
steps.instruction: Provide tailored SMS support for 9 months starting at the 3-month mark for the assigned SMS group.

substeps.instruction: Collect weekly self-monitored SMS data from participants regarding diet, physical activity, and emotions.
Send semi-automated feedback messages reviewed by a mental health professional to provide social support and empowerment.
Send two additional messages per week addressing eating behavior (e.g., portions, emotional eating, sugar-sweetened beverages) and physical activity (e.g., motivation, sedentary behavior).

steps.title: Manage Control Group (Usual Care)
steps.instruction: Provide standard care and encourage weight loss through public services.

substeps.instruction: Schedule 4 consecutive hospital visits for assessments, including short, unstructured consults with a treating physician.
Encourage use of public services (e.g., Weight Watchers, gyms, dieticians) and self-monitoring of diet.
Inform participants of the risks of overweight for mother and child and its relation to fertility.

steps.title: Monitor Outcomes and Eligibility for Treatment
steps.instruction: Measure primary and secondary outcomes at 0, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months and determine eligibility for ovulation induction.

substeps.instruction: Track BMI, reproductive, endocrine, and psychological parameters.
Terminate intervention if a participant misses >3 of 20 group sessions or becomes pregnant.
Qualify control group for ovulation induction if they achieve: weight loss of 4.0 BMI points, BMI < 34.0, and maintenance over 3 months.
Qualify intervention group for ovulation induction if they achieve: weight loss of 4.0 BMI points, BMI < 34.0, and compliance for >1 year.
